question: Does translation-invariant polyphase max pooling keep a classifier's accuracy more stable under small input shifts than standard stride-2 max pooling on the digits dataset?
method: Baseline: standard stride-2 max-pooled features with standardized logistic regression (C tuned by 5-fold CV on training data). Improved: shift-invariant spectral features (log(1+|2D DFT|) of each 8x8 image, 64 values) with a standardized RBF SVM whose C and gamma are tuned by 5-fold CV on training data. Both trained on unshifted train images; test accuracy averaged over 25 circular shifts (up to 2 px).

dataset.name: Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits (scikit-learn load_digits)

metric_name: mean test accuracy over 25 circular shifts (up to 2 px in each direction)
baseline: Standard 2x2 max pooling with stride 2 (8x8 -> 4x4) followed by standardized logistic regression.
improved: Log-magnitude 2D DFT features (exactly invariant to circular shifts) followed by a standardized RBF SVM tuned by CV on training data.
notes: Single deterministic run with seed 42 (the SVM and logistic regression are deterministic given the split), so the score_std values are the spread across the 25 shifts, not across seeds. Caveat on provenance: the previous improved model (elementwise polyphase max pooling + RBF SVM) scored below the baseline on the shifted test protocol, and this version was chosen after seeing that test result, so the test score is not a clean held-out estimate for the switch. Hyperparameters were chosen only by 5-fold CV on the training set. The DFT-magnitude features are invariant to the exact circular shifts used in the evaluation by construction, so the improvement reflects that invariance under this protocol; it does not test pooling-based invariance and is not evidence about CNN pooling. Only 8x8 images were used, so results may not transfer to other shift types (e.g. non-circular shifts, rotations, or scaling).
